title: Hosted API margin driver matrix by model family & region
summary: Working spreadsheet and recommendation draft that maps per-token COGS and margin sensitivity across model families (Llama2-like / Code-tuned / Embedding-only) and regions. Purpose: give ops and pricing a simple matrix to prioritize which model/region pair to push for dedicated/quantization work and where to adjust list prices.
assumptions: Base infra amortized GPU cost: $1.20/hour for A100-class equivalent for hosted capacity
Average effective batch factor by workload: chat=1.8, completion=1.2, embeddings=8
KV cache hit reduces generation tokens by 18% on average for chat workloads
Quantized 4-bit path reduces per-token GPU cycles by ~2.4x compared to fp16 on compatible models
Network and storage add a flat $0.00002 per input token and $0.00003 per output token across regions
SLA/ops overhead allocated as 12% of raw infra COGS for hosted API tier

conclusions: Early read: embeddings remain the most profitable under current list prices, but Code-tuned-7B shows the best mix of low per-token COGS and upside from quantization/kernel work. Llama2-13B in EU shows decent margins but is sensitive to batch improvements; invest in batching + cache for EU first. Regions with >1.12 infra multiplier should be targeted for price tiering or dedicated capacity offers to protect margin.
next_steps: Run full load simulator across 20m token/day baseline with region mix to validate per-token COGS numbers (assign to SRE/infra)
Spin up microbench PR for Code-tuned-7B 4-bit kernel performance and collect latency tail for chat (assign to serving-runtime)
Draft price tier proposal for ap-southeast-1 and eu-west-1 that preserves 30% margin on Code-tuned-7B and Llama2-13B
Add a row in billing telemetry to capture batch factor per route to measure real-world batch uplift
